name: Hydrogen
summary: The lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, powering stars through nuclear fusion.

name: Helium
summary: A colorless, odorless noble gas that remains gaseous down to absolute zero at atmospheric pressure.

name: Lithium
summary: The least dense solid element and lightest metal, essential for modern rechargeable batteries.

name: Beryllium
summary: A relatively rare, stiff, and lightweight metal used in aerospace structures and X-ray tube windows.

name: Boron
summary: A low-abundance metalloid widely utilized in fiberglass, pyrotechnics, and semiconductor doping.

name: Carbon
summary: The chemical basis of all known organic life, capable of forming millions of diverse compounds.

name: Nitrogen
summary: A colorless, odorless gas making up roughly seventy-eight percent of Earth's atmosphere.

name: Oxygen
summary: A highly reactive nonmetal and strong oxidizing agent essential for aerobic cellular respiration.

name: Fluorine
summary: The most chemically reactive and electronegative of all elements, forming compounds with almost everything.

name: Neon
summary: A noble gas known for emitting a distinctive reddish-orange glow in high-voltage electric discharge signs.

name: Sodium
summary: A soft, highly reactive silvery metal that reacts violently with water and forms table salt with chlorine.

name: Magnesium
summary: A lightweight structural metal that burns with an intense white light and plays a central role in chlorophyll.

name: Aluminium
summary: A silvery-white, ductile, lightweight metal that is the third most abundant element in the Earth's crust.

name: Silicon
summary: A hard crystalline metalloid that serves as the foundation of modern semiconductor electronics.

name: Phosphorus
summary: An essential element for life found in DNA, RNA, ATP, and cell membranes, existing in white, red, and black allotropes.

name: Sulfur
summary: A bright yellow nonmetallic solid known since antiquity, vital for cellular amino acids and industrial sulfuric acid.

name: Chlorine
summary: A yellow-green halogen gas widely used for municipal water disinfection and sanitation.

name: Argon
summary: The third most common gas in Earth's atmosphere, frequently used as an inert shielding gas in welding.

name: Potassium
summary: A soft alkali metal critical for biological nerve impulse transmission and intracellular fluid balance.

name: Calcium
summary: A vital mineral essential for building bones and teeth, muscle contraction, and cellular signaling.

name: Scandium
summary: A silvery-white metallic transition metal used in high-intensity stadium lamps and lightweight aerospace alloys.

name: Titanium
summary: A lustrous metal renowned for its exceptional strength-to-weight ratio and outstanding corrosion resistance.

name: Vanadium
summary: A hard, ductile transition metal primarily used to produce high-strength steel alloys for tools and pipelines.

name: Chromium
summary: A steely-gray, lustrous metal that takes a high polish and provides corrosion resistance in stainless steel.

name: Manganese
summary: An essential industrial transition metal critical for iron and steel production and photosynthesis.

name: Iron
summary: The most commonly used metal on Earth by mass, central to steel production and hemoglobin oxygen transport.

name: Cobalt
summary: A magnetic transition metal utilized in blue pigments, superalloys, and lithium-ion battery cathodes.

name: Nickel
summary: A corrosion-resistant silvery-white metal widely used in stainless steel, plating, and rechargeable batteries.

name: Copper
summary: A reddish ductile metal with exceptional electrical and thermal conductivity, used by humans for millennia.

name: Zinc
summary: A versatile metal used to galvanize steel against rust and an indispensable micronutrient in human metabolism.

name: Gallium
summary: A soft silvery metal with a low melting point that literally melts in the warmth of a human hand.

name: Germanium
summary: A lustrous, hard-brittle metalloid crucial in fiber-optic systems, infrared optics, and solar cells.

name: Arsenic
summary: A notorious metalloid used historically as both a potent poison and an alloying agent in lead car batteries.

name: Selenium
summary: A nonmetal with photovoltaic properties used in photocells, glassmaking, and vital dietary enzymes.

name: Bromine
summary: The only nonmetallic liquid element at room temperature, possessing a reddish-brown color and pungent vapor.

name: Krypton
summary: A noble gas used in fluorescent lamps, high-speed photography flash units, and insulated double-pane windows.

name: Rubidium
summary: A highly reactive, soft alkali metal that ignites spontaneously in air and is utilized in laser cooling research.

name: Strontium
summary: An alkaline earth metal known for giving fireworks and emergency road flares their brilliant crimson red color.

name: Yttrium
summary: A silvery transition metal used in high-temperature superconductors, white LEDs, and camera lenses.

name: Zirconium
summary: A lustrous, corrosion-resistant metal widely employed in nuclear reactor fuel cladding due to low neutron absorption.

name: Niobium
summary: A ductile transition metal used in superconducting magnets for MRI scanners and particle accelerators.

name: Molybdenum
summary: A refractory metal with an exceptionally high melting point, prized in high-strength military and aviation steels.

name: Technetium
summary: The lowest-atomic-number element without stable isotopes, widely used in nuclear medicine diagnostic scans.

name: Ruthenium
summary: A rare platinum-group transition metal utilized in wear-resistant electrical contacts and industrial catalysts.

name: Rhodium
summary: An ultra-rare, highly reflective noble metal primarily deployed in automotive catalytic converters.

name: Palladium
summary: A rare, lustrous silvery-white metal capable of absorbing up to 900 times its volume in hydrogen gas.

name: Silver
summary: A precious metal boasting the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any known element.

name: Cadmium
summary: A toxic bluish-white metal historically used in rechargeable nickel-cadmium batteries and protective plating.

name: Indium
summary: A remarkably soft, malleable post-transition metal essential for indium tin oxide touchscreen coatings.

name: Tin
summary: A silvery malleable metal known since antiquity, used in bronze alloys, soldering, and protective plating for cans.

name: Antimony
summary: A lustrous gray metalloid utilized in flame-retardant materials, lead-acid car batteries, and microelectronics.

name: Tellurium
summary: A brittle, mildly toxic metalloid commonly paired with cadmium in thin-film solar panel semiconductors.

name: Iodine
summary: A dark purple-black halogen solid that sublimes into violet gas, indispensable for human thyroid health.

name: Xenon
summary: A dense noble gas utilized in high-intensity arc lamps, deep-space ion propulsion thrusters, and medical anesthesia.

name: Caesium
summary: A soft, golden-tinted alkali metal whose atomic resonant vibration defines the international SI standard second.

name: Barium
summary: A reactive alkaline earth metal utilized in petroleum drilling fluids and medical gastrointestinal contrast radiography.

name: Lanthanum
summary: The namesake of the lanthanide series, used in hybrid vehicle battery electrodes and high-refraction camera lenses.

name: Cerium
summary: The most abundant rare earth metal, commonly found in automotive catalytic converters and glass polishing agents.

name: Praseodymium
summary: A soft malleable metal used in high-strength aircraft engine alloys and specialized welder's goggles.

name: Neodymium
summary: A crucial magnetic metal used to manufacture the most powerful commercial permanent magnets on Earth.

name: Promethium
summary: An entirely radioactive lanthanide used in atomic batteries for pacemakers and luminous navigational instruments.

name: Samarium
summary: A rare earth metal used in high-temperature samarium-cobalt magnets and nuclear reactor control rods.

name: Europium
summary: A ductile lanthanide prized for its red luminescence in fluorescent television screens and anti-counterfeit banknotes.

name: Gadolinium
summary: A metal with remarkable magnetic properties, used as a contrast medium in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

name: Terbium
summary: A rare earth element that produces brilliant green phosphors in sonar sensors and low-energy lighting.

name: Dysprosium
summary: A metal with one of the highest magnetic strengths, added to neodymium magnets to withstand extreme heat.

name: Holmium
summary: A soft malleable metal possessing the highest magnetic moment of any naturally occurring element.

name: Erbium
summary: A bright pink-ion metal used in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers to boost intercontinental optical data signals.

name: Thulium
summary: The second-rarest naturally occurring lanthanide, used as a radiation source in portable medical X-ray units.

name: Ytterbium
summary: A soft silvery metal utilized in high-precision atomic clocks and stress gauges for earthquake monitoring.

name: Lutetium
summary: The final and densest lanthanide element, utilized in positron emission tomography (PET) scan detectors.

name: Hafnium
summary: A corrosion-resistant transition metal used in nuclear submarine control rods and plasma cutting torches.

name: Tantalum
summary: A dense refractory metal vital for manufacturing miniature electronic capacitors in modern smartphones.

name: Tungsten
summary: A robust metal with the highest melting point of all metals, widely used in incandescent filaments and cutting tools.

name: Rhenium
summary: An exceptionally dense refractory transition metal essential in nickel-based superalloys for jet engine turbines.

name: Osmium
summary: The densest naturally occurring element, twice as dense as lead, used in fountain pen nibs and electrical contacts.

name: Iridium
summary: The most corrosion-resistant metal known, famous for the thin geological layer marking the dinosaur extinction event.

name: Platinum
summary: A prestigious, unreactive precious metal extensively utilized in automotive catalytic converters and fine jewelry.

name: Gold
summary: A treasured precious metal that does not tarnish, highly prized for monetary reserves, jewelry, and corrosion-free circuitry.

name: Mercury
summary: The only metallic element liquid at standard conditions, used historically in barometers, thermometers, and fluorescent lamps.

name: Thallium
summary: A soft, highly toxic post-transition metal historically used in rodenticides and low-temperature thermometers.

name: Lead
summary: A heavy, malleable metal utilized since antiquity for radiation shielding, plumbing, and lead-acid storage batteries.

name: Bismuth
summary: A post-transition metal with an iridescent oxidized surface and very low toxicity, used in pharmaceuticals.

name: Polonium
summary: A rare, intensely radioactive metalloid discovered by Marie Curie, used as an alpha-radiation heat source.

name: Astatine
summary: The rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, with less than an ounce existing globally at any given moment.

name: Radon
summary: A radioactive, colorless noble gas formed by the radioactive decay of uranium in soils and underground rock formations.

name: Francium
summary: The second-rarest naturally occurring element, an extraordinarily unstable alkali metal with a half-life of 22 minutes.

name: Radium
summary: An intensely radioactive alkaline earth metal discovered by the Curies, used historically in self-luminous watch dials.

name: Actinium
summary: The namesake of the actinide series, a soft silvery radioactive metal that glows with a faint blue light in the dark.

name: Thorium
summary: A naturally radioactive metal more abundant than uranium, considered a promising fuel source for future nuclear power.

name: Protactinium
summary: A dense radioactive actinide metal with an intense radiological toxicity, used primarily for basic scientific research.

name: Uranium
summary: A heavy radioactive actinide metal that serves as the primary fissile fuel for commercial nuclear power generation.

name: Neptunium
summary: The first synthetic transuranic element ever synthesized, acting as a precursor in the production of plutonium-238.

name: Plutonium
summary: A synthetic fissile actinide metal widely used in nuclear power reactors and radioisotope thermoelectric generators.

name: Americium
summary: A synthetic radioactive actinide metal commonly used in ionizing residential smoke detectors.

name: Curium
summary: A synthetic radioactive metal named in honor of Marie and Pierre Curie, used as an alpha source in space rovers.

name: Berkelium
summary: A synthetic radioactive actinide produced in minute quantities for synthesizing heavier superheavy elements.

name: Californium
summary: A powerful neutron emitter utilized in portable neutron radiography, mineral exploration, and cancer therapy.

name: Einsteinium
summary: Discovered in the radioactive fallout of the first thermonuclear explosion, named in tribute to Albert Einstein.

name: Fermium
summary: The heaviest element that can be formed by neutron bombardment of lighter elements, named after Enrico Fermi.

name: Mendelevium
summary: A synthetic radioactive element synthesized atom-by-atom, named in honor of periodic table creator Dmitri Mendeleev.

name: Nobelium
summary: A synthetic radioactive metal produced using particle accelerators, named in honor of dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel.

name: Lawrencium
summary: The final element of the actinide series, named in memory of Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron accelerator.

name: Rutherfordium
summary: A synthetic superheavy transition metal named in honor of nuclear physics pioneer Ernest Rutherford.

name: Dubnium
summary: A synthetic transition metal named after the Russian research center Dubna where it was first produced.

name: Seaborgium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in honor of Glenn Seaborg, the first living scientist so commemorated.

name: Bohrium
summary: A synthetic superheavy metal named after Danish physicist Niels Bohr, a founder of quantum atomic theory.

name: Hassium
summary: A synthetic superheavy transition metal named after Hesse, the German state hosting the discoverer's laboratory.

name: Meitnerium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in honor of Lise Meitner, co-discoverer of nuclear fission.

name: Darmstadtium
summary: A synthetic superheavy metal named after the city of Darmstadt, Germany, where it was created in 1994.

name: Roentgenium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named after Wilhelm RÃ¶ntgen, the discoverer of X-rays.

name: Copernicium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in tribute to astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.

name: Nihonium
summary: The first chemical element discovered in Asia, named after 'Nihon', the Japanese word for Japan.

name: Flerovium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in honor of Soviet nuclear physicist Georgy Flyorov.

name: Moscovium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in honor of the Moscow region of Russia.

name: Livermorium
summary: A synthetic superheavy element named in honor of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California.

name: Tennessine
summary: A synthetic superheavy halogen named after the US state of Tennessee in recognition of its scientific research centers.

name: Oganesson
summary: The heaviest element on the periodic table, a synthetic superheavy noble gas named after nuclear physicist Yuri Oganessian.
